summary: GCC15.2 whole-program and API-only 11-trial comparisons found no consistent improvement from O3, AVX2 or both. O3 regressed on alternating maximum input; AVX2 regressed on random maximum input; combined API-only timings regressed. All settings matched independent small references and large baseline output. No source changes or split/OR expansion.

candidate_decisions.reason: Some full-program inputs improve slightly, but alternating maximum input regresses about5%; convolution API-only time stays approximately unchanged. A consistent whole-program benefit is not established.
Maximum random input regresses about2.4%, near-mod improves slightly, and API-only timing does not improve. No consistent vectorization speedup.
Near-mod full program improves, but other whole-program inputs do not consistently improve and large API-only cases regress around1.8-2.1%.

correctness.oracle: Independent all pairs i,j accumulating a[i]*b[j] mod998244353 at i&j; O(4^exponent).
correctness.checked_skip_disabled: GCC four settings each skip + checked + disabled + checked_disabled; Clang skip and checked_disabled.
correctness.large_outputs: All four settings produce byte-identical outputs across all8 profiles. Zero profile additionally matches the independently known all-zero output.

limitations: Ratios describe current frozen source under GCC15.2 on local Intel14900K CPU25; they do not assert judge timings on AMD EPYC.
Small whole-process times include startup and noise; no small-input speedup claim.
Compiler/prelude changes affect complete program code generation; API-only instrumentation is a separate controlled benchmark and its ratios cannot be subtracted from whole-program ratios.
Baseline-control medians expose run-to-run variation. Measurements do not prove all possible workloads; current candidates are rejected due insufficient consistent gain and observed regressions.
online_submission_reason: No library/main/I/O/prelude change adopted; exact current source preserved.
